extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for presenting typefaces: showing font families, point sizes, leading/spacing, style variants, language scripts, special characters, and display settings in a specimen/book. Useful for designers choosing or documenting type for print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface / Font family
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists and demonstrates named typefaces (e.g., CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN, BOOKMAN OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM OLD STYLE, FRENCH OLD STYLE, PORSON GREEK, ANTlQUE GREEK, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the face name and provide specimens in that face to illustrate its character; the page uses many examples (CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN, BOOKMAN OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM BOLD CONDENSED, etc.) so readers can compare designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size (type size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type sizes are explicitly labeled and demonstrated (SIX POINT, EIGHT POINT, TEN POINT, ELEVEN POINT, TWELVE POINT, FOURTEEN POINT, EIGHTEEN POINT, TWENTY POINT, TWENTY-TWO POINT, TWENTY-FOUR POINT, THIRTY POINT, THIRTY-SIX POINT, FORTY-FOUR POINT, FORTY-EIGHT POINT, SIXTY POINT, SEVENTY-TWO POINT, NINETY-SIX POINT, ONE-HUNDRED-AND-EIGHTY POINT, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the same sample text at multiple point sizes so readers can judge readability, weight, and display presence; the specimen shows sizes from 6pt upward to very large display sizes (180pt+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading / spacing: 'Leaded' versus 'Solid'
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples are marked {Leaded} or [Solid] to indicate the interline spacing used for the specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the face appears with different leading (tighter 'solid' setting vs looser 'leaded') because line spacing affects readability and texture of a paragraph; label specimens accordingly as the page does (e.g., {Leaded}, [Solid]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Style variants (italic, bold, condensed, wide, bold condensed, italic bold, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specimen differentiates style variants such as ITALIC, ITALIC ITALIC (e.g., CASLON OLD STYLE ITALIC), BOLD, BOLD CONDENSED, WIDE, CONDENSED, BOLD ITALIC, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include separate specimens for each variant (italic, bold, condensed, wide, etc.) and show identical sample lines so designers can compare face rhythm and emphasis across styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample text selection and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A running prose passage ('When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...') is repeatedly used across faces and sizes; display lines such as 'THE FIRST TIME THAT THE GRAND PROSPECT HAD BEEN HELD FORTH' are used for uppercase/title display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a substantive prose paragraph to demonstrate body-text behaviour and longer text flow, and use an uppercase/headline line to demonstrate display/titling; repeat the same copy across specimens to enable direct comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script and language support (Greek, Hebrew, Syriac, Arabic, Ethiopic, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes non‑Latin script specimens labeled PORSON GREEK, ANTIQUE GREEK, INSCRIPTION GREEK, HEBREW, NESTORIAN SYRIAC, ARABIC, ETHIOPIC, showing how faces render other alphabets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide script-specific specimens (ancient and modern forms) to show glyph shapes, diacritic behavior, and suitability for multilingual typesetting; include multiple point sizes for these scripts as done on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters and accented letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections explicitly titled 'ACCENTED LETTERS—SIX TO TWELVE POINT' and 'SPECIAL CHARACTERS— A SIZE' display accent marks and unusual glyphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a dedicated block showing accented characters and special letters across relevant sizes so potential users can verify diacritic design, kerning, and legibility for languages that require accents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals and figure styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerals are shown repeatedly (1234567890) in various faces and sizes as part of the specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show numerals in both body and display sizes to evaluate figure weight, tabular lining vs oldstyle behavior, and to check alignment and spacing in numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous signs and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: A block titled 'MISCELLANEOUS SIGNS' displays mathematical symbols, punctuation, and other signs (e.g., =, +, <, ×, various composed sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate punctuation, currency symbols, math signs, and other special glyphs to ensure completeness of the character set and consistent design across symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uppercase/display titling
rubrics_metrics.description: Uppercase display lines (e.g., 'THE FIRST TIME THAT THE GRAND PROSPECT HAD BEEN HELD FORTH') are set at many display sizes to show capital-letter color and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide uppercase titling specimens at multiple display sizes to check letterspacing, temperament of caps in headlines, and overall visual weight in display contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface family coverage across widths/weights
rubrics_metrics.description: The specimen shows the same family across condensed, wide, bold, bold condensed, and other width/weight permutations (e.g., CHELTENHAM WIDE, CHELTENHAM CONDENSED, CHELTENHAM BOLD CONDENSED).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the full set of available widths and weights for a family so users can assess internal consistency and pick matching faces for different typographic roles (body, caption, headline).
